name: Saining Xie
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Scaling is not the core basis; the real compute bar for training a new foundation model, as the X2 debate confirmed, is more real than I thought in R1
D01.late_modes: Copying scaling-law tuning is already too late; this kind of engineering has been standardized by big companies

D02.one_line: [synthesized] The RLVR mechanism is outside my publications; the consensus of the X7 debate (mainly about pass@1/sampling efficiency) is background knowledge, not a basis on which I can score

D03.one_line: [synthesized] Long-horizon credit assignment/RSI is outside my publications; the 'infinite game' is a career philosophy, not a technical judgment

D04.one_line: GUI grounding is isomorphic to the question I asked when working on V*; I have no basis to judge scaffolding/harness engineering
D04.late_modes: Writing general scaffolding/harness is already too late; each model generation absorbs it into native capability

D05.one_line: Diagnostic benchmarks are how academia can still create leverage despite a compute disadvantage; the whole X1 table confirmed that evaluation does not create capability but is still a core methodology
D05.late_modes: Building a large general leaderboard is already too late; this kind of infrastructure is being commercialized and absorbed by companies such as Arena

D06.one_line: [synthesized] I have no real-robot or VLA work; spatial reasoning might spill over to embodied evaluation, but the evidence is too weak to score

D07.one_line: [synthesized] I have no diffusion policy/VLA publications; it shares only the sampler with the diffusion in my papers

D08.one_line: Spatial/world representation is still a key bottleneck, but the validation gap at the decision-driving layer, independently confirmed by the X3 and X5 tables, is larger than I thought in R1; it is not just my own academic reservation
D08.late_modes: Treating video generation directly as a 'world model' has already been shown to be problematic: it fails on out-of-distribution physical laws
D08.conflict: Co-founder and chief scientist of AMI Labs; equity and funding narrative are staked here

D09.one_line: [synthesized] My publications do not cover physics simulators or sim2real, so there is no public position to cite

D10.one_line: [synthesized] I have no autonomous-driving publications and no basis to judge

D11.one_line: The quality of visual/spatial representation, not language-model reasoning, is the real bottleneck of multimodal systems; ten years of work have confirmed this repeatedly
D11.late_modes: Chasing scores on existing MLLM leaderboards is already too late; the next model generation absorbs them within three months
D11.conflict: This is the foundation of his reputation

D12.one_line: The race for image quality is already commoditized; replacing the VAE with external representations and making generation a by-product of understanding is a subproblem that is still open
D12.late_modes: Chasing plain FID/quality rankings is already too late; it has been absorbed by a price war among a few well-funded companies
D12.conflict: This is the foundation of his reputation

D13.one_line: [synthesized] My publications do not cover mechanistic interpretability or alignment, and I have no basis to judge

D14.one_line: Not my core field; the faster training of REPA/RAE is a by-product of the choice of representation, not systems engineering itself

D15.one_line: [synthesized] I have no AI for Science publications or public position, so I make no judgment

D16.one_line: [synthesized] I have no publications on recommendation/retrieval systems, so I make no judgment

lever_reason: Representation/architecture paradigms are still the deepest bottleneck (L6); the evaluation methodology was confirmed as more solid by the X1/X3 debates, so raised (L1); the validation gap at the layer where world models make decisions is unfilled, so lowered (L4)

Q2.condition: A narrow-domain model + credible third-party evaluation + team and compute at scale (confirmed by the X2 debate) + open weights with a path to outside adoption

cruxes.question: Will diagnostic benchmarks, as a weapon, soon be countered by the same playbook, driving their marginal value to zero?
cruxes.my_position: Still works, but the window is narrowing: Cambrian-S was rebutted within ten days, and X3 also confirmed that D08 lacks an equivalent diagnostic yardstick
cruxes.would_change_if: Two more independent teams' diagnostic benchmarks being rebutted just as quickly within the next year

cruxes.question: Is AMI Labs' JEPA world-model route the necessary continuation of a methodology, or the founder's optimistic narrative?
cruxes.my_position: The whole X3 table independently confirmed that the evidence gap at the decision-driving layer is unfilled; the reader should calibrate this independently
cruxes.would_change_if: AMI Labs ships a usable product within a year, or conversely still has 'no product yet'

cruxes.question: Is diffusion policy the same research problem as the diffusion in my papers?
cruxes.my_position: No, they share only the sampler; robot decision-making addresses a different problem, and I have not published related work
cruxes.would_change_if: Someone shows that a specific technical breakthrough in generative image/video modeling transfers directly and improves robot policy performance

taste_advice: Do not rush into a hot topic that already has its foundational work; find a component or assumption that everyone uses but nobody has verified, and run a small, sharp diagnostic experiment

pairwise.why: The validation gap at the decision-driving layer is unfilled (X3 consensus); the evaluation methodology is more solid right now
I have a real track record in evaluation science; I have none in embodied AI
D08 is still an extension of my ten years of work; I have no track record in D06
D07 is not my direction; D08 is still an extension of my ten years of work
Robot learning is the final proving ground for whether representations can actually be used
Continual learning/memory is closer to a representation problem than RL mechanisms are
Diagnostic questions about understanding are still open; the race for generation quality is commoditized
The debate confirmed the bar for general pre-training is higher; evaluation is where academia really has an edge
I have an analogy for the grounding subproblem inside D04; I have no foundation at all in D03
Interpretability is not my field; evaluation is a methodology I have validated
Embodied AI at least has spatial-reasoning spillover to draw on; I have no foundation at all in autonomous driving

changes.argument_restated: When training a genuinely new foundation model (not a recombination), the team-and-compute bar may be necessary alongside evaluation
changes.why: Narrow, controlled designs (Web-SSL) remain a counterexample; the scope is limited to high-dimensional settings like D06-D08; R3 confirms keeping the downward revision made in round C

changes.because: summary/X3.md consensus: the imagination layer has a third-party yardstick and the decision-driving layer does not; valuations such as AMI Labs' run ahead of validation
changes.argument_restated: The layer at which representations drive decisions was independently confirmed by both the X3 and X5 tables as not yet validated
changes.why: This is a new argument that only came from reading the X3 table, where I did not sit, not a case of 'others changed too'; two tables independently converged on the same gap, and that should show in the confidence

held_despite.why: Accepted that the decline in judge credibility is a fact, but it only hits LLM-judge-style evaluation, not MMVP/AlphaFold2-style diagnostic evaluation

Accepted that D07 is defined as jointly predicting observations and actions, not learning an independent representation first and then attaching a head, but this is only a terminological refinement and does not change that representation quality is still the variable that sets the ceiling

still_disagree: Still disagree on which of D07/D08 deserves a bet now: the existing real-robot evidence (LBM, OpenVLA-OFT) does not separate the two variables of representation quality and action-head design, so we cannot rule out that both sides depend on good representations.
learned: The X3 table's breakdown is more precise than my own general talk of 'readable ≠ usable': the imagination layer has a third-party yardstick and the decision-driving layer does not; I had not explicitly thought of this two-layer distinction before.
